newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-PATRIOTS COACH PARCELLS TO LEAVE TEAM - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-PATRIOTS COACH PARCELLS TO LEAVE TEAM - PAPER.

text.p: Win or lose the Super Bowl, New England Patriots head coach Bill Parcells will leave the team when his contract expires after the season, the Boston Globe reported on Monday.

Sources told the newspaper that Parcells will not return to the Patriots because of his deteriorating relationship with owner Bob Kraft, including the coach's desire to have full control over the team and a dispute over his contract.
Kraft, Parcells and the team flew to New Orleans on Sunday to prepare for Super Bowl XXXI on Jan. 26 against the Green Bay Packers and could not be reached for comment.
Parcells has repeatedly declined to talk about his future, but his departure was widely expected by many Boston sports columnists.
The New York Jets are rumoured to be interested in signing Parcells, the Globe said.

Kraft reportedly believes there is certain language in the contract, which expires on Feb. 1, by which he can require Parcells to coach for the 1997 season for a salary of $1.3 million, the newspaper said.
Parcells' agent Robert Fraley told the newspaper that Kraft told him he would seek compensatation from any National Football League team that attempts to sign Parcells.
Boston sports columnists have speculated that compensation would be in the form of draft picks, and the Jets have the first pick in this year's college draft, the Globe said.

The coach and owner had a major dispute last summer during the college draft when Parcells wanted to select a defensive lineman but Kraft and the team's director of player personnel, Bobby Grier, overruled him and picked Ohio State receiver Terry Glenn.
